analysis.title: Market Barometer November 2026
key_insights: CCLA makes no change to its Barometer this month and holds an overall neutral view: market up, earnings up, valuation flat, growth stable, expected rate hikes unchanged, sentiment still stretched.
Half way through Q3 earnings season (225 of 500 S&P 500 companies reported), revenue growth is 12% versus a usual 5-6% near nominal GDP, and EPS growth is 28%, about 4x the long-run average.
Tech sector revenue has grown 40% and EPS 85%, but consensus had priced most of it in. Revenue and EPS surprises were 1.7% and 2.2%, around half the usual size.
Several Tech stocks that merely met expectations fell 10-20% on the day, which CCLA reads as a lot already in price and expectations.

The MS AI Enablers basket (79 stocks, half Semis and Tech Hardware) has retraced 25% since end of June, while the AI Disrupted basket has rallied 45% over the same period. Nearly half of the enablers' outperformance since late 2023 has been given back.
CCLA thinks it is too soon to call a turning point for AI outperformance. It keeps significant exposure to AI winners but is underweight relative to its comparator and some peers.

CCLA worries about CFROI on AI capex and is selectively underweight the group, even though the top line is growing. Hyperscalers are expected to double invested capital in five years, and PE ratios are falling.
Census Bureau data shows 23% of US businesses use AI in any business function, with a steadily rising trend. Cloud revenue growth is stable at Azure and accelerating at the other major providers.
The US 10-year yield has been driven unusually strongly by short-term rate expectations. Before the US bombed Iran the market expected Fed funds to end 2026 at 3%, and it now expects above 4%.

CCLA sees little value in 10-year Treasuries unless the market starts pricing rate cuts. It argues the Fed should not run policy rates much below 5% given 5% nominal GDP growth and a price level well above target.

Five leading UK Quality equity funds have seen AUM fall 32% since end-2021 while weighted average NAV rose over 23%, meaning 55% of initial assets have been redeemed. The outflow continues at a steady rate.

Quality flows will likely only turn when earnings and revenue upgrades for AI names outside the Quality basket break. Quality index earnings, cashflow growth and yields are strong but below the AI universe.
US flash composite PMI reached 57.6, supported by services and new orders. Markets expect three Fed hikes over 12 months while still anticipating a soft landing.

The UK Budget was a continuation of policy: about £7bn of near-term loosening is offset by roughly equal tightening by 2031-32. Gilt yields fell 1-2bps and sterling was flat on a trade-weighted basis.

French OAT spreads widened a further 17bps against 10-year Bunds in October, after an 80bps rise since June. Foreign investors hold about 60% of OATs. French equities fell 2.7%, and IG and HY spreads widened 14bps and 47bps. CCLA sees little prospect of fiscal improvement before the election.

The October tech sell-off was triggered by disappointing OpenAI revenue news, CoreWeave debt concerns and renewed questions over AI returns. CCLA reads it as a crowded-positioning unwind, not a macro shift: US Momentum fell 13% and high beta 22%, while quality, value and defensives gained.

In US credit, sovereign yields account for about 85% of all-in yields, shifting risk from spreads to rates volatility. Heavy long-duration tech issuance raised duration sensitivity of higher-rated issuers, and A-rated credit has underperformed B/BB.

US corporate profit share of GDP is just off its highest since 1929, earnings are as far above long-run trend as any time since 1929, and non-financial debt is very elevated. Mean reversion could leave US 10-year forward returns well below levels implied by equity risk premiums.

tension_points.bull_case: AI top line is growing and accelerating as adoption goes mass market, with cloud revenue growth stable at Azure and accelerating elsewhere, and Q3 Tech EPS up 85%.
tension_points.bear_case: CFROI on the AI capex build is unlikely to match legacy capital-light returns as hyperscalers double invested capital in five years, and PE ratios are de-rating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break in the trend of ever-rising, upgraded revenue and earnings growth for AI names would end the Quality outflows and shift leadership.

tension_points.bull_case: The market prices Fed funds above 4% by end-2026 versus 3% before the Iran strike, which supports higher yields.
tension_points.bear_case: CCLA thinks the Fed should not run rates much below 5%, so the 10-year offers little value unless the market prices rate cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The market starting to price in interest rate cuts.
